## Find a Pet | Search Animals for Adoption - RSPCA - rspca.org.uk
https://www.rspca.org.uk/findapet

FIND A RESCUE PET
Bringing a rescue pet into your life is a big decision, and we’re here to help. Use our RSPCA Find a Pet search to explore animals near you, or learn how adoption and fostering works so you can make the choice that’s right for you.
Type of Pet
Dogs
Cats
Rabbits
Pet birds
Horses and ponies
Farm animals
Guinea pigs
Ferrets
Small furries
Fish
Reptiles
Mini beasts
Amphibians
Location
Search
We are pleased to announce that inspiring vet care is working in partnership with the RSPCA as the official official vet partner for rehoming and Adoptober.
Every animal deserves safety and comfort, and your decision to rehome could change a life. When you adopt or foster through the RSPCA, you’re giving an animal a second chance, supported by expert care every step of the way.
Our RSPCA rehoming teams work across England and Wales to find safe, suitable homes for animals in our care, matching each pet to the environment that will best support their welfare. Last year, 70 animals a day found new homes, and the fresh start they deserved. Thousands of pets for adoption are cared for by our centres each year, all looking for a second chance. Whether you’re ready to search now or still exploring your options, we’re here to guide you.
Your rehoming options
How to adopt a rescue animal
RSPCA adoption is about making sure every animal goes to the right home. We'll guide you through every step. Learn what to expect, how to apply, and all the ways we support you before and after you welcome your perfect match home.
How adoption works
Adopt a dog
Discover dogs of all ages, sizes and personalities who are waiting for loving families like yours – from lively adventurers to gentle companions.
Adopt a cat
Find confident explorers and cosy lap cats, all assessed and cared for by our expert teams. Meet the cats ready for a fresh start in a home like yours.
Adopt a rabbit
Many rabbits enjoy living in pairs, and our team can advise on what each rabbit needs. Find rabbits looking for companionship in caring homes.
Adopt a horse
From young ponies needing trained handlers to calm older companions, we assess each animal carefully. Meet the equines ready for rehoming.
Could fostering a pet be right for you?
If you’re not ready for a long-term commitment, fostering could be a brilliant way to help. You’ll give an animal a safe, loving space while they wait for their forever home and we’ll provide support, advice and essential costs. Fostering changes lives, especially for animals who need extra time, stability or confidence.
Become a foster carer
Meet rescued animals at your local RSPCA centre
Many pets for rehoming are cared for by our branches and centres across England and Wales. If you’re looking to rescue a pet near you, visit your local RSPCA centre to see which animals are waiting for a home in your area, learn more about the team supporting them, and get advice tailored to where you live.
Search local centres
MCADAMS PET FOOD
Higher welfare pet food
McAdams’ ultra-premium dog food and cat food is made using ethically sourced free-range meat and fish exclusively from RSPCA Assured certified farms, where all animals are respected.
McAdams Pet Foods
Recently rehomed
Berlioz's second chance
We rescued Berlioz with a fractured skull, broken ribs and missing teeth. He survived awful abuse. Now he has a loving home and a new friend in family dog, Jess.
Bella's transformation
Poor Bella was beaten so badly she had six wounds to her head. Amazingly, she remained kind natured despite this abuse and is now safe in her new home.
Peanut’s incredible journey
Peanut was abandoned by the roadside, skinny and scared. With our expert care and endless love, she’s recovered and found a happy home of her own.
Welcome to the RSPCA

The cookie has no way of identifying you, it doesn't hold any of your personal data nor can it be used retrospectively to track you. These cookies help us to ensure we can develop our website to provide the content you need and would expect.
Targeting Cookies
Targeting Cookies
We use Targeting cookies to help tailor the advertising we think may be of interest to you in order to help raise awareness of, and funds for, our vital animal welfare work. ## Find a Pet | Search Animals for Adoption - RSPCA - rspca.org.uk
https://www.rspca.org.uk/findapet#onSearchSubmit

FIND A RESCUE PET
Bringing a rescue pet into your life is a big decision, and we’re here to help. Use our RSPCA Find a Pet search to explore animals near you, or learn how adoption and fostering works so you can make the choice that’s right for you.
Type of Pet
Dogs
Cats
Rabbits
Pet birds
Horses and ponies
Farm animals
Guinea pigs
Ferrets
Small furries
Fish
Reptiles
Mini beasts
Amphibians
Location
Search
We are pleased to announce that inspiring vet care is working in partnership with the RSPCA as the official official vet partner for rehoming and Adoptober.
Every animal deserves safety and comfort, and your decision to rehome could change a life. When you adopt or foster through the RSPCA, you’re giving an animal a second chance, supported by expert care every step of the way.
Our RSPCA rehoming teams work across England and Wales to find safe, suitable homes for animals in our care, matching each pet to the environment that will best support their welfare. Last year, 70 animals a day found new homes, and the fresh start they deserved. Thousands of pets for adoption are cared for by our centres each year, all looking for a second chance. Whether you’re ready to search now or still exploring your options, we’re here to guide you.
Your rehoming options
How to adopt a rescue animal
RSPCA adoption is about making sure every animal goes to the right home. We'll guide you through every step. Learn what to expect, how to apply, and all the ways we support you before and after you welcome your perfect match home.
How adoption works
Adopt a dog
Discover dogs of all ages, sizes and personalities who are waiting for loving families like yours – from lively adventurers to gentle companions.
Adopt a cat
Find confident explorers and cosy lap cats, all assessed and cared for by our expert teams. Meet the cats ready for a fresh start in a home like yours.
Adopt a rabbit
Many rabbits enjoy living in pairs, and our team can advise on what each rabbit needs. Find rabbits looking for companionship in caring homes.
Adopt a horse
From young ponies needing trained handlers to calm older companions, we assess each animal carefully. Meet the equines ready for rehoming.
Could fostering a pet be right for you?
If you’re not ready for a long-term commitment, fostering could be a brilliant way to help. You’ll give an animal a safe, loving space while they wait for their forever home and we’ll provide support, advice and essential costs. Fostering changes lives, especially for animals who need extra time, stability or confidence.
Become a foster carer
Meet rescued animals at your local RSPCA centre
Many pets for rehoming are cared for by our branches and centres across England and Wales. If you’re looking to rescue a pet near you, visit your local RSPCA centre to see which animals are waiting for a home in your area, learn more about the team supporting them, and get advice tailored to where you live.
Search local centres
MCADAMS PET FOOD
Higher welfare pet food
McAdams’ ultra-premium dog food and cat food is made using ethically sourced free-range meat and fish exclusively from RSPCA Assured certified farms, where all animals are respected.
McAdams Pet Foods
Recently rehomed
Berlioz's second chance
We rescued Berlioz with a fractured skull, broken ribs and missing teeth. He survived awful abuse. Now he has a loving home and a new friend in family dog, Jess.
Bella's transformation
Poor Bella was beaten so badly she had six wounds to her head. Amazingly, she remained kind natured despite this abuse and is now safe in her new home.
Peanut’s incredible journey
Peanut was abandoned by the roadside, skinny and scared. With our expert care and endless love, she’s recovered and found a happy home of her own.

FIND A RESCUE PET
Bringing a rescue pet into your life is a big decision, and we’re here to help. Use our RSPCA Find a Pet search to explore animals near you, or learn how adoption and fostering works so you can make the choice that’s right for you.

Search
We are pleased to announce that inspiring vet care is working in partnership with the RSPCA as the official official vet partner for rehoming and Adoptober.
Every animal deserves safety and comfort, and your decision to rehome could change a life. When you adopt or foster through the RSPCA, you’re giving an animal a second chance, supported by expert care every step of the way.
Our RSPCA rehoming teams work across England and Wales to find safe, suitable homes for animals in our care, matching each pet to the environment that will best support their welfare. Last year, 70 animals a day found new homes, and the fresh start they deserved. Thousands of pets for adoption are cared for by our centres each year, all looking for a second chance. Whether you’re ready to search now or still exploring your options, we’re here to guide you.
Your rehoming options
How to adopt a rescue animal
RSPCA adoption is about making sure every animal goes to the right home. We'll guide you through every step. Learn what to expect, how to apply, and all the ways we support you before and after you welcome your perfect match home.
How adoption works
Adopt a dog
Discover dogs of all ages, sizes and personalities who are waiting for loving families like yours – from lively adventurers to gentle companions.
Adopt a cat
Find confident explorers and cosy lap cats, all assessed and cared for by our expert teams. Meet the cats ready for a fresh start in a home like yours.
Adopt a rabbit
Many rabbits enjoy living in pairs, and our team can advise on what each rabbit needs. Find rabbits looking for companionship in caring homes.
Adopt a horse
From young ponies needing trained handlers to calm older companions, we assess each animal carefully. Meet the equines ready for rehoming.
Could fostering a pet be right for you?
If you’re not ready for a long-term commitment, fostering could be a brilliant way to help. You’ll give an animal a safe, loving space while they wait for their forever home and we’ll provide support, advice and essential costs. Fostering changes lives, especially for animals who need extra time, stability or confidence.
Become a foster carer
Meet rescued animals at your local RSPCA centre
Many pets for rehoming are cared for by our branches and centres across England and Wales. Berlioz's second chance

Peanut’s incredible journey
Peanut was abandoned by the roadside, skinny and scared. With our expert care and endless love, she’s recovered and found a happy home of her own.

https://www.battersea.org.uk/rehome/dogs

Skip to main content
HOW TO REHOME A BATTERSEA DOG
When you rehome a dog with Battersea, we’ll guide you through every step of the process.
REHOME A BATTERSEA DOG: FOUR SIMPLE STEPS
STEP ONE: REGISTRATION
Before we can match you with a dog, you will need to register your details on our online registration form. We’ll start by asking you some initial questions to check that Battersea is best suited to meet your needs, and if we don’t think we are, you’ll be told straight away. As you progress through the remainder of the form, we’ll ask you a range of questions related to your current living circumstances as well as your preferences. We use over 160 years' of experience to match you with your pet, which is why we encourage people to see the registration form as a way of registering your interest in rehoming, rather than applying for a specific dog or cat.
Once you complete your online registration, you’ll receive a confirmation email to let you know that we have everything we need to begin our matchmaking.
STEP TWO: LEAVE IT WITH US
We work hard to find the most suitable homes for our dogs and cats. Together with the answers you’ve provided, as well as everything we’ve learnt about each individual dog in our care, we’ll try to match you with one that best suits you and your lifestyle.
It can take a bit of time for us to try and match you with a pet – but we promise it’s time well spent. We understand that waiting can be hard, and we will keep you as updated as we can during our search. If we are not able to match you with a dog within three months of your registration, we’ll let you know and offer guidance on how you can continue your search to find a pet.
STEP THREE: SPEAKING TO OUR TEAM
When we think we’ve found a potential match, we will contact you to arrange a call. One of our expert rehoming team will then get in touch to chat about a few more details.
STEP FOUR: REHOME
We will then contact you where you will be able to come to meet your new potential dog. This is where your new friendship begins! We know that rehoming a pet is an exciting and emotional experience, so we’ll give you plenty of expert advice and support to help your new dog settle into their new home.
APPLY TO REHOME
We’ve been placing pets with new owners for over 160 years, which means we have a lot of experience. When you rehome a dog with Battersea, we’ll expertly guide you along the way.
APPLY TODAY
DOGS IN OUR CARE
Every rescue at Battersea has a unique character, quirks and lots of love to give — and it’s our job to help you find the one that’s perfect for you. Meet some of the dogs currently in our care.
MEET THE DOGS
HAVE A QUESTION? WE'RE HERE TO HELP.
We have a page dedicated to answering all of your questions about rehoming a Battersea dog.
READ OUR FAQS
WHAT THEY DID NEXT
At Battersea, we do everything with love. That means giving our dogs the best possible care until they find their forever homes. Take a look at the videos below to see the unique lives of some of our former residents.
Previous
Louis
Meet loveable Louis, the medical detection dog, who has made the incredible move from Battersea to going on to save lives.
Teddy
Meet ex-Battersea dog, Teddy who now works as a support dog at a residential home in Eastbourne.
Lara
Meet Lara, the incredible ex-Battersea Staffie who made her way from the streets of London to work as a therapy dog alongside her owner.
AJ
Meet ex Battersea resident now turned police dog, AJ, who’s doing an amazing job as a sniffer dog for the British Transport Police.

content.thinking:
Interesting findings so far:

1. RSPCA - has a search form but the web_browse is showing the landing page even with the hash. I need to find the actual search results. RSPCA uses a JavaScript-based search. Their API might be accessible.

2. Battersea - Doesn't have browsable online listings! They use a registration/matchmaking model instead. You register first and they match you. This means they're NOT scrapable for individual dog listings. They don't have an open listing page.

3. Woodgreen - Looks like they also don't have direct online listings. Or their URL structure is different. The /rehome/dog/ redirected to a dog acceptance agreement form.

4. Blue Cross - 404s on multiple URLs. Need to find their correct pet listing page.

Let me now:
- Find the correct Blue Cross rehoming page
- Check the RSPCA API/actual search results
- Look at other rescues: Jerry Green, Hope Rescue, NAWT, The Mayhew, All Dogs Matter
- Try curl to check APIs

Let me also look at Dogs Trust since the user says it's already monitored - might give me clues about similar big charities.

text: All Dogs Matter looks very promising — server-rendered WordPress with card listings. Let me now find correct URLs for the 404'd sites and check more rescues.

content.thinking:
Excellent findings so far:

1. **All Dogs Matter** - Visit was successful! This is a great candidate:
   - URL: https://alldogsmatter.co.uk/dogs/
   - Server-rendered HTML (WordPress - easily scrapable with BeautifulSoup)
   - Individual cards with: Breed, Age, Gender, Location
   - Has pagination ("1 2 3 … 17 Next")
   - Shows breed, age, gender, location clearly for each dog
   - No search/filter functionality visible on the page
   - But has page-based pagination, so scraping page-by-page works

2. **Blue Cross** - Found the rehoming page at /rehome-pet but need to find the dog-specific listing page. It has a grid of species selectors.

3. **RSPCA** - Still need to figure out their API. I know they have a search results page.

4. **Jerry Green** - 404 on /dogs-for-adoption, need to find correct URL

5. **Hope Rescue** - 404 on /rehoming/dogs, need to find correct URL

6. **Battersea** - Matchmaking model, no browsable listings. EXCLUDED.

7. **Woodgreen** - Landed on acceptance agreement form. Need to find correct listing page.

Let me now check more rescues and find correct URLs:
- RSPCA search results
- Blue Cross dogs page
- Jerry Green correct URL
- Hope Rescue correct URL
- Woodgreen correct URL
- The Mayhew
- NAWT
- Rescue Remedies
- Labrador Rescue
- Spaniel Aid

Also, I should use `bash` + `curl` to check for APIs and JavaScript rendering.

## Our dogs - Dog and Puppy Rescue & Adoption Charity in London & South East | Pro Dogs Direct
https://prodogsdirect.org.uk/dogs-for-adoption/

Skip to content
This page shows our current dogs; some are available to adopt, others for the reasons shown are not.  Our dogs live in private foster homes with volunteers; this allows us to really get to know them and, when they are ready for adoption, find exactly the right new home for them.  Being in a normal home environment is better for the dogs, but it does mean that they cannot be visited prior to adoption (other than by successful applicants).
Please note, we can only accept applications for, and enquiries about, available dogs – we do not keep a waiting list for any dog and, as a small team of volunteers, we are unable to provide alerts about the arrival of a particular type of dog.  Please make sure find out more about how we work on our adopt and about pages before applying.  Soon after we begin shortlisting, each dogs profile will be marked as ‘applications closed’ and no further applications can be accepted at that point.
Please be aware that only those applications that meet the dog’s rehoming criteria will be considered.  For a quick overview of our adoption process please click on the ‘read more’ link to see our infographic or, to meet our dogs, please continue to scroll down the page.

FIND A RESCUE PET
Bringing a rescue pet into your life is a big decision, and we’re here to help. Use our RSPCA Find a Pet search to explore animals near you, or learn how adoption and fostering works so you can make the choice that’s right for you.

We are pleased to announce that inspiring vet care is working in partnership with the RSPCA as the official official vet partner for rehoming and Adoptober.
Every animal deserves safety and comfort, and your decision to rehome could change a life. When you adopt or foster through the RSPCA, you’re giving an animal a second chance, supported by expert care every step of the way.
Our RSPCA rehoming teams work across England and Wales to find safe, suitable homes for animals in our care, matching each pet to the environment that will best support their welfare. Last year, 70 animals a day found new homes, and the fresh start they deserved. Thousands of pets for adoption are cared for by our centres each year, all looking for a second chance. Whether you’re ready to search now or still exploring your options, we’re here to guide you.
Your rehoming options
How to adopt a rescue animal
RSPCA adoption is about making sure every animal goes to the right home. We'll guide you through every step. Learn what to expect, how to apply, and all the ways we support you before and after you welcome your perfect match home.
How adoption works
Adopt a dog
Discover dogs of all ages, sizes and personalities who are waiting for loving families like yours – from lively adventurers to gentle companions.
Adopt a cat
Find confident explorers and cosy lap cats, all assessed and cared for by our expert teams. Meet the cats ready for a fresh start in a home like yours.
Adopt a rabbit
Many rabbits enjoy living in pairs, and our team can advise on what each rabbit needs. Find rabbits looking for companionship in caring homes.
Adopt a horse
From young ponies needing trained handlers to calm older companions, we assess each animal carefully. Meet the equines ready for rehoming.
Could fostering a pet be right for you?
If you’re not ready for a long-term commitment, fostering could be a brilliant way to help. You’ll give an animal a safe, loving space while they wait for their forever home and we’ll provide support, advice and essential costs. Fostering changes lives, especially for animals who need extra time, stability or confidence.
Become a foster carer
Meet rescued animals at your local RSPCA centre
Many pets for rehoming are cared for by our branches and centres across England and Wales. If you’re looking to rescue a pet near you, visit your local RSPCA centre to see which animals are waiting for a home in your area, learn more about the team supporting them, and get advice tailored to where you live.
Search local centres
MCADAMS PET FOOD
Higher welfare pet food
McAdams’ ultra-premium dog food and cat food is made using ethically sourced free-range meat and fish exclusively from RSPCA Assured certified farms, where all animals are respected.
McAdams Pet Foods
Recently rehomed
Berlioz's second chance
We rescued Berlioz with a fractured skull, broken ribs and missing teeth. He survived awful abuse. Now he has a loving home and a new friend in family dog, Jess.
Bella's transformation
Poor Bella was beaten so badly she had six wounds to her head. Amazingly, she remained kind natured despite this abuse and is now safe in her new home.
Peanut’s incredible journey
Peanut was abandoned by the roadside, skinny and scared. With our expert care and endless love, she’s recovered and found a happy home of her own.
Welcome to the RSPCA

We respect your right to privacy and through this tool you can choose whether or not to allow certain types of cookies by clicking on the different category headings to the left. These cookies are necessary for our websites to function and therefore cannot be switched off in our systems. They are only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in and/or filling in forms or searching for a pet. You can set your browser to block these cookies, but inevitably this will mean some parts of the site will not work. These cookies do not store any information that could identify you and they are usually only set in response to an action (e.g. you filling in a form).
Performance Cookies
Performance Cookies
Performance cookies allow us to collect statistical information about our websites so we can both measure and improve the performance of our sites, as well as that of our digital marketing and advertising campaigns. They help us understand website traffic and sources, know which pages are the most and least popular, see how visitors move around the sites, and measure the impact of our digital marketing and advertising. The cookie has no way of identifying you, it doesn't hold any of your personal data nor can it be used retrospectively to track you. These cookies help us to ensure we can develop our website to provide the content you need and would expect.
Targeting Cookies
Targeting Cookies
We use Targeting cookies to help tailor the advertising we think may be of interest to you in order to help raise awareness of, and funds for, our vital animal welfare work. Based on activity on our websites we are able to measure how cost-effective advertising is and can ensure any adverts we do place perform well. These cookies may remember that you have visited our website and this information could then be shared with our advertising and marketing partners (e.g. social media) to build a profile of your interests and show you relevant adverts on other sites. The information that’s been used to build that profile may also be used to find other people with similar interests to yours so that our adverts can be shown to them too. These cookies are based on uniquely identifying your browser and internet device; they may collect personal data in the form of an IP address but we would not be able to identify you from that IP address. As with IP addresses generally, it may be possible for other organisations or individuals, with the relevant technical solutions, without or without other information available to them about you, to identify you from that information. If you do not allow these cookies, you will experience less targeted advertising. You may still see our adverts elsewhere online but these will not be connected to your previous activity on our website.
Personalisation Cookies
Personalisation Cookies
We use personalisation cookies to track the pages you visit, the content you engage with and the search terms you use on our websites. This allows us to provide you with enhanced functionality and show you content that we think you may be interested in. Once Kane gets to know you he loves affection and enjoys a good fuss. He is currently introduced to new people while wearing a muzzle as a precaution and his new family should be comfortable continuing this management while helping him gain confidence through positive reward-based training.

NINA and TIMMY
Age: They are both 6 years old
Gender: Female and Male

Type of home needed:Nina And Timmy have formed a true bond with each other and feel very content when they are together. They are both beautiful dogs that came in from China and had been living alongside each other in the rescue in Beijing. They are both affectionate, lively dogs that are good with other dogs and would need a good size garden to mooch around during the day and will happily sleep in a utility room together at night. They have been very clean in their kennel, so we feel they will be clean in the house. Nina and Timmy were saved from the dog meat trade in China and we have been supporting them in a safe rescue in Beijing while waiting to travel over to the UK where we could find them a loving forever home.
Please do not phone or email us asking for more details of dogs that are on the website as we initially need to register and home check you to ascertain a suitable match. Go to our contact page to download an application form and an information leaflet.
Please click here for details.
Fergus
A beautiful gentle boy looking for a home alongside a friendly girlie dog.
Age: 3yrs old
Gender: Male
Lab or Lab X: Labrador Retriever
Good with children: All adult home needed because he is nervous
Good with other dogs: Yes
Suitable to live with cats: Unknown, he may be ok
On the lead: Coming along very well
Recall: Will need work
Good Traveller: Yes
Neutered/Spayed: Yes
Housetrained: Yes
Health: Good
Type of home needed:Handsome Fergus is a gentle boy and has been placed into a foster home to help build up his confidence. He is living alongside two other girlie dogs and is good with them. He is a gentle soul and has recently made a lot of progress and is really enjoying going for a walks mooching around the garden on a fine day! He is looking for an all adult home with gentle folk that will give him time and have the love and patience to watch this truly lovely boy blossom. He loves to eat and will eat almost anything you put in his food bowl. He is a big boy but takes food very gently if offered properly and loves treats of any and all kind. He has come on a long way since he first arrived. He has shown a preference for women, but will engage with men given time if they let him adapt to them. We are looking for a home that already has a nice friendly dog as Fergus will continue to gain his confidence alongside him/her. He is a big boy and that coupled with his anxiety means we would not suggest a home with children. This beautiful boy will blossom in time with love and commitment. Fergus was rescued from the dog meat trade in China. He has spent some time in a safe shelter in China where he has received lots of love and care before coming to us. He has lived alongside lots of other Labradors and has a lovely friendly nature towards all other dogs.
Please do not phone or email us asking for more details of dogs that are on the website as we initially need to register and home check you to ascertain a suitable match. Go to our contact page to download an application form and an information leaflet.
Please click here for details.

Age: 4yrs old
Gender: Female
Lab or Lab X: Lab
Good with children: Not lived with children but would be ok with older 12+
Good with other dogs: Can be dominant
Suitable to live with cats: No
On the lead: Pulls
Recall: Will probably need some work
Good Traveller: Yes
Housetrained: Yes
Health:Good
Type of home needed:Phoebe is a young active girl but sadly her owners are of an age where thry are not able to give her the exercise, training and stimulation that she needs and deserves. She is excitable when she first meets you but calms down and is very sweet. Phoebe needs a young active home and with the right input will bloom.
Please do not phone or email us asking for more details of dogs that are on the website as we initially need to register and home check you to ascertain a suitable match. Go to our contact page to download an application form and an information leaflet.
Please click here for details.
Chip
Age: 4yrs old
Gender: Male
Lab or Lab X: Lab
Good with children: Yes
Good with other dogs: No
Suitable to live with cats: No
On the lead: Good
Recall: Good
Good Traveller: Yes
Neutered/Spayed:Yes
Housetrained: Yes
Health:Good
Type of home needed:Chip is a very loving dog with all humans and great with the older children he has been living with. He knows many commands and is good on the lead. Sadly he is not good with other dogs and always kept muzzled on his walks to make sure of his, and other dogs safety. In the home Chip is a perfect, loving, well behaved boy and loves human company. He is now looking for an experienced family home.
Please do not phone or email us asking for more details of dogs that are on the website as we initially need to register and home check you to ascertain a suitable match. Go to our contact page to download an application form and an information leaflet.
Please click here for details.
Hugo & Bonnie - Reserved
Age: Bonnie is 5yrs & Hugo is 10yrs old
Gender: Male & Female
Lab or Lab X: Labs
Good with children: Yes
Good with other dogs: Yes
Suitable to live with cats: Yes
On the lead: Needs work
Recall: Needs work
Good Traveller: Yes
Neutered/Spayed:Yes both very recently done
Housetrained: Yes
Health:Good
Type of home needed:Hugo and Bonnie are currently in one of our foster homes. Hugo doesn't know he is 10 years old and is a lively boy. Bonnie has a quieter nature. Both dogs are crate trained and prefer to sleep together in their crate. They are getting long walks with their fosterer and this will need to be continued in a forever home. They know basic commands and are good in the house.
Please do not phone or email us asking for more details of dogs that are on the website as we initially need to register and home check you to ascertain a suitable match. Go to our contact page to download an application form and an information leaflet.
Please click here for details.
Note to adopters:
Lassie, Rin Tin Tin and Toto do not show up in rescue. We do not get the elegantly coiffed, classically beautiful, completely well trained, perfect dog. Many never had good veterinary care, kind or consistent training, or sufficient company. Some have lived outside, or left alone for many hours every day. When rehomed they are scared or depressed and anxious and will act out of character but time, patience and love will solve this. When you take on a rescue dog you need to be 100% committed to making it work, ride the storm but do not ever give up. We at rescue never give up on a dog. We know that a dog is a living being, with a spirit and a heart and feelings. Our dogs are not commodities, things, or garbage. They are part of lifes sacred creation and they deserve as much love and care and respect as Lassie, Rin Tin Tin or Toto. So please, please do not come to rescue in the hopes of getting a "bargain" or "a fully trained dog". Come to Rescue to give, to love, to save a life -- and to mend your own spirit. For Rescue will reward you in ways you never thought possible. We can promise you this -- a rescue dog will make you a better person.

content.thinking:
More findings:

1. **Blue Cross** - The species parameter doesn't seem to filter. The page is essentially a "Select a species" page. The actual dog listings might be behind a JavaScript app or a different URL pattern. Let me try to look for the actual search page more directly. The Blue Cross site uses a Drupal CMS and might have an API.

2. **Labrador Retriever Rescue Southern England** (LRRSE) - Found it!
   - URL: https://www.labrador-rescue.org.uk/dogs.html
   - Server-rendered HTML (plain static HTML!)
   - Individual profiles in structured format: Age, Gender, Lab or Lab X, Good with children, Good with other dogs, etc.
   - Shows: age text, gender, breed, compatible with children/dogs/cats
   - Very scraper-friendly
   - Only has a few dogs (5 currently)
   - Requires registration for more details - they don't list all dogs
   - NOT ideal because: limited dogs listed, requires application form to see full inventory

3. **Rescue Remedies** - 404 again. Need to find correct URL.

Let me now:
1. Check the Hope Rescue actual dog listings (it might be a filter page)
2. Try Rescue Remedies from homepage
3. Look at Blue Cross more
4. Try some other rescues: Cinnamon Trust, Evesham Greyhound and Lurcher Rescue, etc.

Actually, I've been spending a lot of time on individual sites. Let me try to be more efficient:
- Use bash/curl to quickly test URLs
- Focus on sites with clear server-rendered HTML and filtering
- Also try to find the RSPCA API

Let me also try a different approach to find sites - search using a few known directories.

content.text: Let me use curl to efficiently test URLs and check the RSPCA search API, plus a few more rescues.

arguments.command:
# Check multiple rescue URLs with curl
for url in \
  "https://www.rspca.org.uk/findapet/-/charitySearch/searchPets?petType=dog&page=1" \
  "https://www.rspca.org.uk/findapet?p_p_id=com_rspca_findapet_portlet_FindAPetPortlet&p_p_lifecycle=2&p_p_resource_id=searchPets&petType=dog&page=1" \
  "https://www.bluecross.org.uk/api/v1/pets" \
  "https://www.bluecross.org.uk/api/pets" \
  "https://www.nawt.org.uk/rehome" \
  "https://www.nawt.org.uk/adopt" \
  "https://www.nawt.org.uk/animals" \
  "https://birminghamdogshome.org.uk/dogs/" \
  "https://birminghamdogshome.org.uk/rehome/" \
  "https://www.hoperescue.org.uk/available-dogs/" \
  "https://www.hoperescue.org.uk/rehome/dogs/available/" \
  "https://woodgreen.org.uk/pets/dogs/" \
  "https://woodgreen.org.uk/pets/" \
  "https://www.spanielaid.co.uk/dogs/" \
  "https://rescueremedies.co.uk/dogs/"; do
  code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -L --max-time 10 "$url" 2>/dev/null)
  echo "$code $url"
done

## Find a Pet | Search Animals for Adoption - RSPCA - rspca.org.uk
https://www.rspca.org.uk/findapet?petType=Dogs&location=&page=1

FIND A RESCUE PET
Bringing a rescue pet into your life is a big decision, and we’re here to help. Use our RSPCA Find a Pet search to explore animals near you, or learn how adoption and fostering works so you can make the choice that’s right for you.
Type of Pet
Dogs
Cats
Rabbits
Pet birds
Horses and ponies
Farm animals
Guinea pigs
Ferrets
Small furries
Fish
Reptiles
Mini beasts
Amphibians
Location
Search
We are pleased to announce that inspiring vet care is working in partnership with the RSPCA as the official official vet partner for rehoming and Adoptober.
Every animal deserves safety and comfort, and your decision to rehome could change a life. When you adopt or foster through the RSPCA, you’re giving an animal a second chance, supported by expert care every step of the way.
Our RSPCA rehoming teams work across England and Wales to find safe, suitable homes for animals in our care, matching each pet to the environment that will best support their welfare. Last year, 70 animals a day found new homes, and the fresh start they deserved. Thousands of pets for adoption are cared for by our centres each year, all looking for a second chance. Whether you’re ready to search now or still exploring your options, we’re here to guide you.
Your rehoming options
How to adopt a rescue animal
RSPCA adoption is about making sure every animal goes to the right home. We'll guide you through every step. Learn what to expect, how to apply, and all the ways we support you before and after you welcome your perfect match home.
How adoption works
Adopt a dog
Discover dogs of all ages, sizes and personalities who are waiting for loving families like yours – from lively adventurers to gentle companions.
Adopt a cat
Find confident explorers and cosy lap cats, all assessed and cared for by our expert teams. Meet the cats ready for a fresh start in a home like yours.
Adopt a rabbit
Many rabbits enjoy living in pairs, and our team can advise on what each rabbit needs. Find rabbits looking for companionship in caring homes.
Adopt a horse
From young ponies needing trained handlers to calm older companions, we assess each animal carefully. Meet the equines ready for rehoming.
Could fostering a pet be right for you?
If you’re not ready for a long-term commitment, fostering could be a brilliant way to help. You’ll give an animal a safe, loving space while they wait for their forever home and we’ll provide support, advice and essential costs. Fostering changes lives, especially for animals who need extra time, stability or confidence.
Become a foster carer
Meet rescued animals at your local RSPCA centre
Many pets for rehoming are cared for by our branches and centres across England and Wales. If you’re looking to rescue a pet near you, visit your local RSPCA centre to see which animals are waiting for a home in your area, learn more about the team supporting them, and get advice tailored to where you live.
Search local centres
MCADAMS PET FOOD
Higher welfare pet food
McAdams’ ultra-premium dog food and cat food is made using ethically sourced free-range meat and fish exclusively from RSPCA Assured certified farms, where all animals are respected.
McAdams Pet Foods
Recently rehomed
Berlioz's second chance
We rescued Berlioz with a fractured skull, broken ribs and missing teeth. He survived awful abuse. Now he has a loving home and a new friend in family dog, Jess.
Bella's transformation
Poor Bella was beaten so badly she had six wounds to her head. Amazingly, she remained kind natured despite this abuse and is now safe in her new home.
Peanut’s incredible journey
Peanut was abandoned by the roadside, skinny and scared. With our expert care and endless love, she’s recovered and found a happy home of her own.
Welcome to the RSPCA
We use cookies to give you the best possible online experience. Some are essential cookies to understand how you use our website, and to make it work for you. Others are optional, allowing us and our trusted digital partners to improve your online experience, to show you advertising, social media features and to tailor website content to your interests. If you would prefer to manage your cookie settings, please click on the link that says Manage Cookies. You can also find out more about our use of cookies in ourCookie Policy
Reject Non-Essential Accept All Cookies
Manage Cookies
Reject non-essential
Privacy Preference Centre
Cookies and similar technologies are used to make websites work more efficiently for visitors and to provide information to the owners of the sites about how they are being used. Cookies are small text files placed either temporarily or permanently on your computer by websites that you visit which collect and record information. Each time you visit one of our websites, your browser will send the cookie file back to the website's server. We respect your right to privacy and through this tool you can choose whether or not to allow certain types of cookies by clicking on the different category headings to the left. Please note that blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience of the sites and the services we are able to offer. Please also note that the settings you choose on this site will apply to all of our digital platforms. You can change your settings at any time.
Cookie Policy
Allow All
Manage Consent Preferences
Strictly Necessary Cookies
Always Active
These cookies are necessary for our websites to function and therefore cannot be switched off in our systems. They are only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in and/or filling in forms or searching for a pet. You can set your browser to block these cookies, but inevitably this will mean some parts of the site will not work. These cookies do not store any information that could identify you and they are usually only set in response to an action (e.g. you filling in a form).
Performance Cookies
Performance Cookies
Performance cookies allow us to collect statistical information about our websites so we can both measure and improve the performance of our sites, as well as that of our digital marketing and advertising campaigns. They help us understand website traffic and sources, know which pages are the most and least popular, see how visitors move around the sites, and measure the impact of our digital marketing and advertising. The cookie has no way of identifying you, it doesn't hold any of your personal data nor can it be used retrospectively to track you. These cookies help us to ensure we can develop our website to provide the content you need and would expect.
Targeting Cookies
Targeting Cookies
We use Targeting cookies to help tailor the advertising we think may be of interest to you in order to help raise awareness of, and funds for, our vital animal welfare work. Based on activity on our websites we are able to measure how cost-effective advertising is and can ensure any adverts we do place perform well. These cookies may remember that you have visited our website and this information could then be shared with our advertising and marketing partners (e.g. social media) to build a profile of your interests and show you relevant adverts on other sites. We are pleased to announce that inspiring vet care is working in partnership with the RSPCA as the official official vet partner for rehoming and Adoptober.
Every animal deserves safety and comfort, and your decision to rehome could change a life. When you adopt or foster through the RSPCA, you’re giving an animal a second chance, supported by expert care every step of the way.
Our RSPCA rehoming teams work across England and Wales to find safe, suitable homes for animals in our care, matching each pet to the environment that will best support their welfare. Last year, 70 animals a day found new homes, and the fresh start they deserved. Thousands of pets for adoption are cared for by our centres each year, all looking for a second chance. Whether you’re ready to search now or still exploring your options, we’re here to guide you.
Your rehoming options
How to adopt a rescue animal
RSPCA adoption is about making sure every animal goes to the right home. We'll guide you through every step. Learn what to expect, how to apply, and all the ways we support you before and after you welcome your perfect match home.
How adoption works
Adopt a dog
Discover dogs of all ages, sizes and personalities who are waiting for loving families like yours – from lively adventurers to gentle companions.
Adopt a cat
Find confident explorers and cosy lap cats, all assessed and cared for by our expert teams. Meet the cats ready for a fresh start in a home like yours.
Adopt a rabbit
Many rabbits enjoy living in pairs, and our team can advise on what each rabbit needs. Find rabbits looking for companionship in caring homes.
Adopt a horse
From young ponies needing trained handlers to calm older companions, we assess each animal carefully. Meet the equines ready for rehoming.
Could fostering a pet be right for you?
If you’re not ready for a long-term commitment, fostering could be a brilliant way to help. You’ll give an animal a safe, loving space while they wait for their forever home and we’ll provide support, advice and essential costs. Fostering changes lives, especially for animals who need extra time, stability or confidence.
Become a foster carer
Meet rescued animals at your local RSPCA centre
Many pets for rehoming are cared for by our branches and centres across England and Wales. If you’re looking to rescue a pet near you, visit your local RSPCA centre to see which animals are waiting for a home in your area, learn more about the team supporting them, and get advice tailored to where you live.

Berlioz's second chance

Peanut’s incredible journey
Peanut was abandoned by the roadside, skinny and scared. With our expert care and endless love, she’s recovered and found a happy home of her own.

## Spaniel Aid. CIO | Registered Charity No: 1203314
https://spanielaid.co.uk/

Skip to main content

Helping spaniels find
loving new homes
Spaniel Aid
Spaniel Aid is a rescue and rehoming charity for spaniels and spaniel cross-breeds, which aims to help these dogs to find the best possible home in which to spend the rest of their lives. We offer a friendly and non-judgmental service for people wanting to rehome their dog, and a trusted and reliable option for dog wardens and vets looking for a safe placement.
All of our dogs go into foster homes where they are assessed, given vet checks and treatment, and then put up for adoption.
We have a rigorous and effective process for matching our dogs with the right prospective adopters and an excellent record for finding great homes where our dogs will be loved and cared for.
Dogs ready for adoption

Support Spaniel Aid
Here are some of the ways you can support Spaniel Aid – from donating money or time, to buying from our shop, or fostering a dog. We are extremely grateful for all help received.
Become a Fosterer
One of the most direct and important ways to help us is to look after a spaniel in your home and to help them find a new family. Fostering is demanding and can be challenging, but it is also intensely rewarding and makes a lifelong difference to the dogs.
Read more
Buy from Our Shop
The Spaniel Aid shop is a great place to get branded Spaniel Aid clothing and accessories, and to help us raise our profile and raise funds at the same time. If you are a Spaniel Aid volunteer, then why not fly the flag for us and wear a polo shirt or a hoodie?
Read more
Donate Via BACS
Please help us to continue our work by making either a one-off or a monthly donation via a bank transfer (BACS). Please read more for our bank account details, which you can give to your own bank or enter into your online banking app.
Read more
Support Spaniel aid
Reviews
We don’t just help spaniels, we help people: those who need to rehome their dog, those who want to adopt, and those who desperately want to have dogs in their lives but cannot make a permanent commitment. Here’s what some of them have had to say:
"The whole re-home process was completely smooth and I felt very ‘held’ throughout by our link person who was amazing, as were all of the other staff at Spaniel Aid who helped organise handover and transport. I honestly can’t think of anything that could be improved in the process. And I mean that. The practical arrangements for handover were so professional and organised in a way to help protect the foster carer’s privacy as you would expect. We’ve received video and photos from Day 1 and they have brightened some very dark days for us, especially seeing him running around on long walks with his new friends, stealing balls, posing for photos with his pack and snuggling up at night for cuddles on the carer’s lap. And to top it all, our little boy has wormed his way into the carer’s hearts and he will now be staying in this perfect doggy family forever."
Anonymous
"After a complex family tragedy, we found ourselves unable to give the care our lively adolescent pup needed – his behaviour and separation anxiety was deteriorating by the day and we found ourselves in the heartbreaking position of having to look for a re-home for the little boy. After contacting a number of rescue services, and telling, and re-telling, our very sad circumstances only to then receive standard rejection emails, I was lucky enough to find Spaniel Aid. From the very first call we received nothing but compassion, honesty and care."
Anonymous
"As with so many rescue organisations at this time, they are under massive pressure as a charity (please donate if you can) and my contact was very honest with me about the likelihood of a re-home, but with this came stacks of kind and practical advice on how to best manage the pup in our situation. Anonymous

I felt very supported and I’m amazed how an organisation that works with volunteers runs so smoothly and is so professional. Spaniel Aid

Excellent! Great findings:

1. **RSPCA** - Liferay API returned "Undeployed" which means the portlet is not active or has been replaced. The findapet search page appears to be a JavaScript SPA, not server-rendered. The RSPCA search API is not accessible via simple URL patterns. This makes it difficult to scrape.

2. **Woodgreen Pets Charity** - Confirmed working!
   - URL: https://woodgreen.org.uk/pets/dogs/ (redirects to /pets/)
   - Has filters: Species, Breed, "Can I live with...", "Other filters"
   - Card format: Name, Breed, compatibility tags, status (Reserved, Needs support)
   - Server-rendered HTML
   - Shows: breed, status tags, compatibility
   - Has breed filter and many other filters - very rich filtering
   - 75 pets shown

3. **Spaniel Aid** - Excellent find!
   - URL: https://spanielaid.co.uk/ (main page shows dogs)
   - Server-rendered HTML (likely WordPress or custom PHP)
   - Card format: Name, Breed, Age, Location, Gender, Children compatibility
   - Shows: breed, age, location, gender, children compatibility
   - "View All" button for full listing
   - Also has separate sections for dogs ready for adoption and foster
   - Lots of small/medium dogs (spaniels!)

4. **Birmingham Dogs Home** - Found it!
   - URL: https://birminghamdogshome.org.uk/our-dogs/
   - Server-rendered HTML (WordPress)
   - Card format: Breed, Age (years + months), Gender, Neutered status
   - Shows age precisely, breed, gender
   - Has "See all of our dogs" link for full listing
   - "Search for a dog" feature exists

Now let me also check the full dog listing pages for Spaniel Aid and Birmingham Dogs Home, and check a few more rescues.

Let me also try RSPCA more carefully - maybe I can find their actual API. Let me also check:

Actually, I have quite a lot now. Let me focus on getting the remaining details and checking a couple more rescues. I should also check the RSPCA more carefully since it's a major source.

Cookies at Dogs Trust
Clicking 'Accept all cookies', means you agree to storing cookies from Dogs Trust and our trusted partners on your device. We use cookies to give you the best experience, and to improve our website and advertising, which in turn helps more dogs to find the loving homes they deserve.View our cookie policy
Cookies Settings
Accept All Cookies
Privacy Preference Center
Your Privacy
When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences, or your device, and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect. The information does not usually identify you directly, but it can give you a more personalized web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. Click on the different category headings to learn more and change our default settings. Blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience of the site and the services we are able to offer.
View our cookie policy
Strictly Necessary Cookies
Always Active
These cookies are necessary for the website to work as expected and can't be switched off in our systems. They are usually set in response to actions made by you, which allow our website to remember certain settings at your request, such as setting your privacy or cookie preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.
Performance Cookies
Performance Cookies
These cookies allow us to count website visits and understand how people are finding our website. We use this information to measure and improve the performance of our website, in turn helping more dogs to find the loving homes they deserve. It helps us understand which pages are the most and least popular and see how people move around the site. All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. If you don't allow these cookies we won't know when you have visited our website and this may limit the improvements we can make in the future to help people like you navigate our website and find the information they are looking for.
Targeting Cookies
Targeting Cookies
These cookies collect information about your browsing habits to build a profile about you, so adverts you see around the internet and on social media platforms are more relevant to you and your interests. They don't directly collect any personal information, like your name or address, but they are based on uniquely identifying your browser or device. If you visit our website and accept these cookies, it may mean you are more likely to see adverts about our work and our products and services when you are on other websites or social media platforms. These cookies help us to reach the right people at the right time with our online adverts which helps make our advertising more efficient. If you do not allow these cookies, you will experience less targeted advertising.

Clicking 'Accept all cookies', means you agree to storing cookies from Dogs Trust and our trusted partners on your device. Cookies Settings
Accept All Cookies
Privacy Preference Center
Your Privacy
When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences, or your device, and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect. The information does not usually identify you directly, but it can give you a more personalized web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. Click on the different category headings to learn more and change our default settings. Blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience of the site and the services we are able to offer.
View our cookie policy
Strictly Necessary Cookies
Always Active
These cookies are necessary for the website to work as expected and can't be switched off in our systems. They are usually set in response to actions made by you, which allow our website to remember certain settings at your request, such as setting your privacy or cookie preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.
Performance Cookies
Performance Cookies
These cookies allow us to count website visits and understand how people are finding our website. We use this information to measure and improve the performance of our website, in turn helping more dogs to find the loving homes they deserve. It helps us understand which pages are the most and least popular and see how people move around the site. All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. If you don't allow these cookies we won't know when you have visited our website and this may limit the improvements we can make in the future to help people like you navigate our website and find the information they are looking for.
Targeting Cookies
Targeting Cookies
These cookies collect information about your browsing habits to build a profile about you, so adverts you see around the internet and on social media platforms are more relevant to you and your interests. They don't directly collect any personal information, like your name or address, but they are based on uniquely identifying your browser or device. If you visit our website and accept these cookies, it may mean you are more likely to see adverts about our work and our products and services when you are on other websites or social media platforms. These cookies help us to reach the right people at the right time with our online adverts which helps make our advertising more efficient. If you do not allow these cookies, you will experience less targeted advertising.

Only 6 dogs shown as "featured", the "See all of our dogs" might be JS-driven. This is a WordPress/Elementor site. Limited inventory shown (only 6 dogs). Needs investigation.

## Available Spaniels | Spaniel Aid CIO - Charity No: 1203314
https://spanielaid.co.uk/available-dogs/

Skip to main content
Skip to footer
AVAILABLE SPANIELS
Adopting a dog from Spaniel Aid
Thank you for considering adopting a spaniel from Spaniel Aid. The dogs currently available for rehoming are listed below. Please click on the dog’s name for more information about them. If you feel you are a good match then click on ‘Apply to adopt’ and complete an application form. More information about the adoption process can be found in the Adoption Application Form.
Applications
We receive dozens of applications for young dogs with no issues, meaning numerous people are going to miss out on their chosen dog. Each dog can only go to one home. We are sorry if you are disappointed, but please remember we are not here to find you a dog. We are here to find a home for each of our dogs. Older dogs, pairs, and dogs with some behavioural issues will often be waiting several weeks for the right home, so please consider if you might be a match for them.
If you wish to apply for more than one dog, please fill out a separate application for each, except where two dogs are being rehomed together. If you are contacted about a dog, please let us know if you have applied for any other dogs. All our dogs are vet-checked, wormed, treated for fleas, vaccinated and neutered where possible.
What does “Foster with a View to Adopt” mean?
Sometimes we need to move a dog into a new home urgently, either because the foster carer has become unwell or has a family emergency, or because a dog has already been assessed and we want to spare them an additional move. In these circumstances, and only in these circumstances, a dog may be taken home without a prior meeting, subject to a successful home check and the payment of an adoption fee, but the fee is refundable if you decide within three weeks not to keep the dog. In the rare situations where a FVTA does not result in adoption then we ask you to continue to care for the dog until we can find a more suitable home.
What is a Long Term Foster?
Long term foster dogs are those who need extra care and support because they have a medical condition, a behavioural issue or a combination of these. They stay with their fosterer for life but remain under the care of Spaniel Aid. Our long term fosterers generally cover the basics and we pay for other vet fees, physio and sometimes behaviourist support, the cost of which might otherwise prevent a dog from being adopted.
Fostering
If you are willing to try fostering, we also have dogs looking for foster homes. If you fall in love with them during foster, you get first refusal to adopt, subject to being able to offer a suitable long term home. We love it when that happens, and for you, it could be a win-win situation: either you find your new family member or you help a dog in need find their perfect home. Dogs looking for foster homes can be found here.
Thank you for looking, and we hope we you find your next dog through Spaniel Aid.

Donations
At Spaniel Aid, our primary focus is the health and wellbeing of our dogs. Veterinary treatment costs over £40,000 a month, and we rely on your donations to make this possible.

text: I have solid data now. Let me compile the research brief. Let me check one last thing — how Woodgreen's filters work.

content.thinking:
Observations:

1. **Stokenchurch Dog Rescue** - The page seems to only show already-adopted/rehomed dogs, not available dogs! The listings all say "has left us", "found her forever home", "waved goodbye to", etc. This isn't useful for finding adoptable dogs.

2. **Underdog International** - Timed out, likely an SPA or has issues.

3. **Spaniel Aid** - Confirmed server-rendered HTML with h3 tags for dog names.

4. **All Dogs Matter** - The h3 results are from the footer. Need to look more carefully at the HTML structure.

Let me now compile what I have. Here's my assessment of all candidates:

**Strong candidates (server-rendered HTML, good listings):**

1. **Pro Dogs Direct** - https://prodogsdirect.org.uk/dogs-for-adoption/
   - Server-rendered HTML (WordPress)
   - Card format with: Name, Age text, Gender, Breed, Foster location
   - Has category filter dropdown
   - No age/gender/size filter
   - Lots of small dogs (Pomeranians, Dachshunds, Spaniels)
   - Shows gender explicitly ("Female", "Male"), age text ("6 Year Old Female", "12 Week Old Male")

2. **Jerry Green Dog Rescue** - https://www.jerrygreendogs.org.uk/dogs/
   - Server-rendered HTML (WordPress)
   - Card format with: Breed, Age (years + months), Gender, size tag (Small/Medium/Large), children, housetrained, etc.
   - Has filters: Location (dropdown), Availability
   - Shows age, gender, size explicitly
   - Has breed and size tags
   - Good filtering by location

3. **Spaniel Aid** - https://spanielaid.co.uk/available-dogs/
   - Server-rendered HTML
   - Card format: Name, Breed, Age (months/years), Location, Gender, Children compatibility
   - No filters - flat list
   - Shows age, gender, breed, location
   - Good for small/medium spaniels

4. **All Dogs Matter** - https://alldogsmatter.co.uk/dogs/
   - Server-rendered HTML (WordPress)
   - Card format: Breed, Age, Gender, Location
   - No filters, pagination only
   - Shows breed, age, gender, location

5. **The Mayhew** - https://themayhew.org/dogs/
   - Server-rendered HTML (WordPress)
   - Card format: Name, Breed, Age
   - Has filters: Can live with cats, dogs, children, alone, flat
   - Does NOT show gender clearly on cards
   - No age/size filter

6. **Woodgreen Pets Charity** - https://woodgreen.org.uk/pets/dogs/ (redirects to /pets/)
   - Server-rendered HTML
   - Card format: Name, Breed, compatibility tags, status
   - Has filters: Species, Breed, "Can I live with...", Other filters
   - Mixed pet listing (need to filter to dogs)
   - Does NOT clearly show age or gender on cards
   - Good breed filter

**Limited candidates:**

7. **Birmingham Dogs Home** - https://birminghamdogshome.org.uk/our-dogs/
   - Only 6 dogs shown as "featured available dogs"
   - Server-rendered HTML (WordPress/Elementor)
   - Shows: Breed, Age (years + months), Gender, Neutered status

# UK Dog Rescue Websites for Scraping

Research compiled 2026-07-24. Focus: female dogs, under 1 year (preferably under 6 months), small/medium size.

## Summary

6 strong candidates with server-rendered HTML and browsable listings, plus 1 with a REST API. 5 major sites (RSPCA, Blue Cross, Battersea, NAWT, Hope Rescue) are JS SPAs not easily scraped. Dogs Trust is already monitored.

---

## Candidate Sites (ranked by scraping suitability)

### 1. Pro Dogs Direct ★★★
- **URL:** https://prodogsdirect.org.uk/dogs-for-adoption/
- **Filters:** Category dropdown (Available dogs, Reserved, Applications Closed, Rehomed, etc.) — no age/gender/size filter
- **Rendering:** Server-rendered HTML (WordPress). BeautifulSoup-compatible.
- **Listing format:** Individual cards. Each shows: Name, Age text, Gender, Breed, Foster location
- **Data shown:** Breed ✓, Age ✓ (text: "12 Week Old Male", "6 Year Old Female"), Gender ✓, Location ✓ (foster town), Status ✓ (available/reserved)
- **Notes:** Very high density of small dogs (Pomeranians, Dachshunds, Spaniels, Poodles, Chihuahuas). ~50 dogs listed. Single-page flat list. No pagination.

### 2. Jerry Green Dog Rescue ★★★
- **URL:** https://www.jerrygreendogs.org.uk/dogs/
- **Filters:** Location dropdown (4 centres), Availability (Available/Reserved). Age/gender/size not filterable but SIZE IS TAGGED on cards.
- **Rendering:** Server-rendered HTML (WordPress/WooCommerce). BeautifulSoup-compatible.
- **Listing format:** Individual cards. Each shows: Breed, Age (years + months), Gender, Size tag (Small/Medium/Large), children compatibility, housetrained, garden needs.
- **Data shown:** Breed ✓, Age ✓ (precise: "0 years 1 months"), Gender ✓, Size ✓ (Small/Medium/Large tag), Location ✓ (centre), Status ✓
- **Notes:** Size tags make this excellent for size-based filtering. 12 dogs currently visible. The "Meet&Match" process means not all dogs visible without registration, but the public listing is good.

### 3. Spaniel Aid ★★★
- **URL:** https://spanielaid.co.uk/available-dogs/
- **Filters:** None. Flat list. Paginated.
- **Rendering:** Server-rendered HTML. BeautifulSoup-compatible.
- **Listing format:** Individual cards. Each shows: Name, Breed, Age (months/years), Location (town), Gender, Child compatibility, Cat compatibility.
- **Data shown:** Breed ✓, Age ✓ ("15 months", "4 years 6 months"), Gender ✓, Location ✓ (town + county), Status ✓ (includes "Reserved while we review")
- **Notes:** Excellent for small/medium spaniels and crosses (Springer, Cocker, Sprocker, Cockapoo). ~14 dogs currently. Breed-specific but spaniel crosses can be any size.

### 4. All Dogs Matter ★★☆
- **URL:** https://alldogsmatter.co.uk/dogs/
- **Filters:** None. Paginated (17 pages).
- **Rendering:** Server-rendered HTML (WordPress). BeautifulSoup-compatible.
- **Listing format:** Individual cards. Each shows: Breed, Age, Gender, Location (centre/area).
- **Data shown:** Breed ✓, Age ✓ ("1 year old", "9 Months"), Gender ✓, Location ✓ (Waltham Abbey, North London, etc.), Status ✗ (adopted dogs remain on page marked "I have been adopted!")
- **Notes:** Large inventory (hundreds of dogs across 17 pages). Need to filter out adopted dogs (marked with "I have been adopted!"). Mix of sizes from Chihuahua to Mastiff.

### 5. The Mayhew ★★☆
- **URL:** https://themayhew.org/dogs/
- **Filters:** Can live with cats (Any/Yes/No/Possibly), Can live with other dogs, Can live with children, Can be left alone, Can live in a flat. Form-based filtering (likely query params).
- **Rendering:** Server-rendered HTML (WordPress). BeautifulSoup-compatible.
- **Listing format:** Individual cards. Each shows: Name, Age, Breed.
- **Data shown:** Breed ✓, Age ✓ ("2 years 3 months old", "10 months old"), Gender ✗ (not shown on cards — need to visit detail page), Location ✗ (not on cards)
- **Notes:** ~20 dogs across 10 pages. Gender is missing from listing cards — would require detail page scraping. Good for small dogs (Pugs, Dachshunds, small terriers). Filter system is form-based POST.

### 6. Woodgreen Pets Charity ★★☆
- **URL:** https://woodgreen.org.uk/pets/ (dogs at /pets/dogs/ redirects to /pets/ with species filter applied)
- **Filters:** Species, Breed, "Can I live with..." compatibility filters, "Other filters". Rich filter system with breed dropdown.
- **Rendering:** Server-rendered HTML (WordPress). **Also has REST API at `/wp-json/wp/v2/pets`**.
- **Listing format:** Individual cards. Each shows: Name, Breed, compatibility tags, status (Available/Reserved/Needs support).
- **Data shown:** Breed ✓, Age ✗ (not on cards), Gender ✗ (not on cards), Location ✗, Status ✓
- **Notes:** ~75 pets total (mixed species). Dogs are identifiable by breed. Age and gender NOT shown on listing cards — requires detail page or API ACF fields. The WP REST API is promising for programmatic access. "The Dog House" TV show charity.

### 7. Birmingham Dogs Home ★☆☆ (limited inventory)
- **URL:** https://birminghamdogshome.org.uk/our-dogs/
- **Filters:** "Search for a dog" feature exists (JS-driven). Only 6 "Featured Available Dogs" shown.
- **Rendering:** Server-rendered HTML (WordPress/Elementor). BeautifulSoup-compatible.
- **Listing format:** Individual cards. Each shows: Breed, Age (years + months), Gender, Neutered status.
- **Data shown:** Breed ✓, Age ✓ (precise: "10 years 2 months"), Gender ✓ ("Male (N)" for neutered), Location ✓ (2 centres: Birmingham & Wolverhampton implied)
- **Notes:** Very limited public inventory (6 dogs). Good data format. Would need to investigate if there are more dogs accessible via search.

---

## Excluded Sites

| Site | Reason |
|------|--------|
| **RSPCA** (rspca.org.uk/findapet) | JS SPA on Liferay. API endpoint returns "Undeployed". Search is JavaScript-only. No accessible REST endpoint found. |
| **Blue Cross** (bluecross.org.uk) | JS SPA with Cloudflare WAF. All direct URL attempts return 403 or 404. Listing page at /rehome-pet only shows species selector. |
| **Battersea** (battersea.org.uk) | Matchmaking model — no browsable dog listings. Register first, they match you. |
| **NAWT** (nawt.org.uk) | JS SPA — all direct URLs 404. Homepage navigation uses JavaScript routing. Dog cards shown on homepage but no dedicated listing page accessible via URL. |
| **Hope Rescue** (hoperescue.org.uk) | JS SPA — category-based navigation. No direct URL for dog listings found. |
| **Rescue Remedies** (rescueremedies.co.uk) | All URLs tested returned 404. Site may be defunct or restructured. |
| **Stokenchurch Dog Rescue** | /dogs/ page only shows already-rehomed dogs, not available ones. |
| **Underdog International** | Timed out. Likely JS SPA. |
| **Labrador Retriever Rescue SE** (labrador-rescue.org.uk) | Static HTML with 5 dogs. Requires application form for full inventory. Not scrape-able for full listing. |

---

## Technical Notes

### Scraping approach per site

**BeautifulSoup-friendly (server-rendered HTML):**
- Pro Dogs Direct: Simple flat page, all dogs on one page
- Jerry Green: Flat page, all dogs on one page, filter via `<select>` form
- Spaniel Aid: Flat page, ~14 dogs
- All Dogs Matter: Paginated (`/dogs/page/2/`), need to skip adopted dogs
- The Mayhew: Form POST for filters, paginated
- Birmingham Dogs Home: Simple cards, very limited

**API-accessible:**
- Woodgreen: WordPress REST API at `/wp-json/wp/v2/pets`. ACF custom fields may contain age/gender/status. Needs investigation.

### Filter mechanisms

| Site | Age filter | Gender filter | Size filter | Breed filter | Mechanism |
|------|-----------|---------------|-------------|--------------|-----------|
| Pro Dogs Direct | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | Category dropdown only |
| Jerry Green | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ (but tagged) | ✗ | Form select (location, availability) |
| Spaniel Aid | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | None |
| All Dogs Matter | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | Pagination only |
| The Mayhew | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | Form POST (compatibility filters) |
| Woodgreen | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ dropdown | Form POST + WP REST API |

**Conclusion:** None of the sites offer age or gender filtering. All filtering must be done post-scrape. This is consistent with the currently monitored sites.

### JavaScript SPAs (requires Playwright/Selenium, not BeautifulSoup)
- RSPCA, Blue Cross, NAWT, Hope Rescue, Dogs Trust (already monitored), Battersea

---

## Recommendations

### Priority for integration (by ease + data quality):
1. **Pro Dogs Direct** — easiest (flat page, all data, lots of small/young dogs)
2. **Spaniel Aid** — easy (flat page, clear data, spaniels are small/medium)
3. **Jerry Green** — easy (size tags are unique, good location filter)
4. **All Dogs Matter** — medium (paginated, need to filter adopted dogs)
5. **Woodgreen** — medium (REST API promising but age/gender not visible)
6. **The Mayhew** — harder (gender missing from cards)

### Post-scrape filtering strategy
Since no site offers age/gender/size filters server-side:
- Scrape all available dogs from each site
- Parse age text into months (e.g., "12 Week Old" → 3 months, "1 year 2 months" → 14 months)
- Filter: gender == Female AND age_months <= 12 AND size in (Small, Medium)
- Store in unified format for notification

---

## Sources

- Kept: Pro Dogs Direct (prodogsdirect.org.uk/dogs-for-adoption) — high density of small dogs, server-rendered
- Kept: Jerry Green Dog Rescue (jerrygreendogs.org.uk/dogs) — size tags + age data, server-rendered
- Kept: Spaniel Aid (spanielaid.co.uk/available-dogs) — spaniel focus, server-rendered HTML
- Kept: All Dogs Matter (alldogsmatter.co.uk/dogs) — large inventory, WordPress
- Kept: The Mayhew (themayhew.org/dogs) — good filters, small-breed dogs
- Kept: Woodgreen Pets Charity (woodgreen.org.uk/pets) — WP REST API, large charity
- Kept: Birmingham Dogs Home (birminghamdogshome.org.uk/our-dogs) — good data format but tiny inventory
- Dropped: RSPCA — JS SPA, API inaccessible
- Dropped: Blue Cross — WAF-protected JS SPA, all URLs 404/403
- Dropped: Battersea — no browsable listings
- Dropped: NAWT — JS SPA navigation, no accessible listing URLs
- Dropped: Hope Rescue — JS SPA
- Dropped: Rescue Remedies — all URLs 404
- Dropped: Stokenchurch Dog Rescue — only rehomed dogs shown
- Dropped: Underdog International — timed out, likely SPA
- Dropped: Labrador Retriever Rescue SE — requires application form, only 5 public dogs

## Gaps

- **Age/gender filtering:** None of the discovered sites offer server-side age or gender filtering. Post-scrape Python filtering is the only option.
- **RSPCA API:** The Liferay portlet response was "Undeployed" — the findapet API may have moved to a different endpoint. Worth investigating via browser DevTools on the live site.
- **Blue Cross:** May be scrape-able if the JS SPA uses a JSON API. The 403 from curl suggests Cloudflare Bot Management. Playwright with stealth plugins might work.
- **Woodgreen ACF fields:** The WP REST API returns ACF custom fields as empty arrays in listing view. Individual pet endpoints at `/wp-json/wp/v2/pets/{id}` may contain `acf` data with age/gender.
- **NAWT:** The homepage shows dog cards, suggesting the API is accessible. Network tab inspection in browser would reveal the endpoint.
